title: No Bad Teams, Only Bad Leaders
coreMove: test the leader’s standard before judging the team by changing what the leader models, repeats, and accepts
sourcePressure: The Hell Week boat-crew leader swap shows the same team performing differently when standards and leadership change.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: bad teams do not exist, so leaders can magically fix anything

sourceAnchors.name: Hell Week boat-crew story
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says the same crew performs differently when the leader changes
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Hell Week boat-crew story works because the people stay the same while the leadership variable changes.

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse pick crew with the lowest accuracy on the night shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift supervisor who thinks his crew is lazy
exampleSpecs.stakes: incorrect shipments are threatening a retail contract
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor changes his own start-of-shift standard, demonstrates one clean pick path, audits the first ten orders with the crew, and the error pattern changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a handheld scanner buzzes red over a bin of identical black cables

exampleSpecs.domain: high-school debate squad losing every cross-examination round
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach tempted to blame student confidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: the regional qualifier is two weeks away and the team is spiraling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach records his own vague feedback, replaces it with a three-question cross-exam standard, and drills it until students can run it without him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: creased rebuttal cards spill from a debate tub onto the hallway floor.

exampleSpecs.domain: ambulance dispatch shift with growing call backlog
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatch supervisor hearing complaints about slow trainees
exampleSpecs.stakes: delayed ambulance assignment can put callers at risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor reviews her training gaps, rewrites the escalation rule in plain language, and shadows the next two calls instead of blaming trainees
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: five pending calls stack yellow on the dispatch console.

exampleSpecs.domain: hotel housekeeping floor with repeated room-readiness failures
exampleSpecs.audience: an assistant manager blaming one floor team
exampleSpecs.stakes: guests are arriving before rooms are inspected
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager swaps floor leads for one morning, keeps the same attendants, and watches the inspection score change when the standard is demonstrated differently
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Brass room key envelope waits on the desk while room 814 still shows dirty.

exampleSpecs.domain: student robotics pit failing safety inspection
exampleSpecs.audience: a robotics mentor who thinks the build team lacks discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: the robot cannot compete unless wiring and guards pass inspection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mentor admits he never defined ready, posts a visible inspection standard, demonstrates one compliant wiring run, and assigns peer checks before the next inspection
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: loose battery lead dangles beside a yellow inspection sticker.

exampleSpecs.domain: line-cook station missing ticket times during dinner service
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous-chef frustrated with a quiet new station team
exampleSpecs.stakes: the dining room backs up and plates die in the pass
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sous-chef stops blaming speed, calls the standard at the pass, resets the station layout with the cooks watching, and runs the next five tickets beside them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: ticket rail spits out six chits while sauce skins over under the heat lamp?

skillTargets: diagnose how leader standards shape a team’s performance
avoid labeling a team before testing leadership inputs
choose the leader behavior that changes expectations visibly

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one team complaint you have repeated, then write the standard you have modeled, repeated, and allowed that may be teaching it.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
